gen-gf-sniglet-gf-suse: Soft, rounded, and quietly confident, Sniglet stops its terminals short of curling back in. And SUSE, a sans-serif with open bowls tipped toward you, is the friendlier half of the deal.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-suse-mono: Sniglet's rope-thin outline never swells or pinches, and its terminals stop before they curl, which gives headings a hushed, level beat. SUSE Mono keeps the space generous.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-tajawal: Commanding in an odd, hushed way, Sniglet keeps its arms and legs at constant width above Tajawal's broad open hooks. Bump Tajawal up a size if it feels slight.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-tasa-orbiter: Sniglet has no thick-and-thin contrast to slow the eye, so headings glide past in one smooth sweep. TASA Orbiter, a plain sans, does the opposite job, keeping every tiny counter unclogged.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-teachers: Sniglet leads with terminals that stop short of curling back in, level and unaccented. Teachers, a plain sans like thin steel rod bent into letters, would read lightly and crisply over many lines.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-telex: Telex reads curvy and unclamped, loose in the joints. Sniglet's thin-looking letters, with no thinner parts anywhere, sit above it like a steady, unfussy sign over a relaxed room.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-tenor-sans: Smooth, uniform, and a bit stubborn, Sniglet traces every glyph with one thickness, while Tenor Sans brings a light taper like a sharpened carpenter's pencil. Expect a plain sans that moves along gently.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-tirra: Tirra's round forms read like open parentheses, gentle and modern. But Sniglet is the one that commands, holding a single stroke width where Tirra, a sans-serif, simply lets the text breathe.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-titillium-web: No sparkle here: Sniglet holds a constant stroke weight and stops its terminals short of curling. And Titillium Web, a sans-serif with stroke ends set far apart, gives that restraint some breathing space.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-tomorrow: Distinctive from the first glance, Sniglet keeps horizontals as thick as verticals. Tomorrow, a sans with bowls that open like a cupped palm of clay, softens the page beneath it.
